exposure: GWG outside the 2009 Institute of Medicine (IOM) guidelines
cohort: Singletons without fetal anomalies delivered to women at Taipei Chang Gung Memorial Hospital between 2009 and 2015
finding: The study found that abnormal pregestational BMI and GWG outside the 2009 Institute of Medicine (IOM) guidelines were associated with increased risks of various adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with the specific effects varying by pregestational BMI category.
mod_finding: Women with gestational weight gain above the Institute of Medicine guidelines had higher rates of primary cesarean delivery.
